teams.heading: Jake White moves Fiji's captain's run from the Aviva to Kirwan Park
teams.body: Jake White's Fiji have been training at De La Salle Palmerston FC, the junior club known locally as 'Salmo', and have felt so at home there that they decided to hold their captain's run on Friday at Kirwan Park rather than the Aviva Stadium. Non-playing squad members were due to train at the club again on Saturday morning. Club director of rugby Norman Byrne watched the sessions and said: "They’re the nicest people you’ll ever come across."

teams.heading: Will Joseph's five tries match England record in 78-15 win over Japan
teams.body: Will Joseph's second cap turned into a record-equalling afternoon as the wing crossed five times in England's 78-15 win over Japan on Saturday. Japan were a man down before they touched the ball, Harry Hockings sent off inside the first minute for a dangerous hit on Ellis Genge, and Joseph had a hat-trick inside 20 minutes. Five tries matches the England record held jointly by Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell, and England's 78 points were their biggest total for a quarter of a century.

teams.heading: Julien Marchand ruled out for rest of Nations Championship; Jalibert nears return
teams.body: Planet Rugby understands that Julien Marchand has been ruled out for the rest of the Nations Championship. The hooker felt further thigh tightness in the warm-up before the South Africa win and had to pull out of the starting side, with Peato Mauvaka taking his place and Guillaume Cramont now the reserve hooker. The news is partly offset at fly-half, where Matthieu Jalibert, out since a quadriceps injury on 20 September, is expected at Marcoussis early next week and in line for the squad to face Argentina.

teams.heading: Ryan Baird recalls playing on with broken leg against South Africa
teams.body: Ireland's Ryan Baird played on after a blow to the leg against South Africa at the Aviva Stadium in November 2025, convinced it was a dead leg. He went down, was strapped up, and only an X-ray in the stadium revealed a broken left leg. Tadhg Beirne, by Baird's account, told him to come off if he could not run. A comeback through two URC games and a Heineken Cup quarter-final was then interrupted by a second problem, and Baird says the year was soul-sapping.

teams.heading: Italy fall 19-14 to Argentina after Garbisi's late missed touch kick
teams.body: Italy's Genoa test against Argentina ended 19-14 to the Pumas on Saturday, and the last-minute error was Paolo Garbisi's. Trying to set up a lineout in a scoring position, the flyhalf missed a penalty touch kick, with the Azzurri having spent the closing stages pressing against 14 men after Efraín Elías was yellow-carded. Monty Ioane's early try and a second-half penalty try gave Italy their points. The Pumas won the game with three tries, and Italy remain winless in the competition.

teams.heading: Five-year-old Joey Sharp to deliver Murrayfield match ball for Scotland v Australia
teams.body: Scottish Rugby have arranged for the five-year-old from Midlothian and his mother, Sam Sharp, to meet the Scotland players. Joey was diagnosed with a brain tumour at 11 days old and has had three surgeries and nine rounds of chemo, and he lives with cerebral palsy as a result of his treatment. He will deliver the ball alongside Commonwealth Games swimmer Archie Goodburn, and his mother says he is "buzzing" to meet the team. It will be his first game at Murrayfield, and his mother is a season-ticket holder.

teams.heading: Alex Cuthbert left speechless on BBC commentary as Wales beat All Blacks
teams.body: Former Wales wing Alex Cuthbert could barely contain himself at the final whistle in Cardiff, his emotion captured on BBC Radio 5 Live's footage from the commentary box. Commentator Sara Orchard had called it as the whistle blew: "This is it, this is the moment." Then Cuthbert, his voice broken, said: "Oh my God, I don't know what to say. Wow, what?! Just unbelievable." Wales had earned it: 73 years and 34 consecutive defeats to New Zealand ended in a 35-28 win.

teams.heading: Pumas travel to Paris after a difficult year of five defeats
teams.body: Argentina go to Paris carrying a hard calendar year, and Rugbyrama's preview, written before Saturday's Genoa win, counts only one victory before it, against Wales. France are, in the paper's words, heavily depleted, but they have dominated the head-to-head: they won 37-23 when the teams last met in November 2024. Argentina's last win over France came in 2014, a game in which Nicolás Sánchez landed four drop goals.

teams.heading: Les Kiss recalls Carter Gordon and Rob Valetini, drops Declan Meredith
teams.body: Carter Gordon is back from the broken leg that has been the latest of several injuries to derail his progress, and Les Kiss has restored him to the starting XV for Sunday's Test against Scotland. "Certainly Carter was the incumbent, so he was in a position of strength before he got injured," Kiss said. Rob Valetini is back in the starting side at six, while Declan Meredith, who looked lost in the defeat by England, has been dropped from match-day 23.

teams.heading: Japan had a player sent off before touching ball against England
teams.body: England ran in 13 tries in the 78-15 win at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, and Gerard Meagher's Guardian analysis says Japan's day never got better after the early dismissal. Meagher reads the scoreline as proof of a widening gap between the leading nations and the rest. Japan's tries came from Warner Dearns and Opeti Helu, with Naoto Saito kicking the conversion and penalty.

teams.heading: Warner Dearns, who turned down the All Blacks, co-captains Japan's England match
teams.body: Warner Dearns, a second row raised in New Zealand's Hawke's Bay region, was due to co-captain Japan against England at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. His father Grant took a strength and conditioning job at NEC Green Rockets when Warner was 14, moving the family to a satellite city outside Tokyo, and he went only reluctantly. He made his Japan debut in November 2021, aged 19. This year he spent a season's sabbatical at the Hurricanes, helping Wellington win their first Super Rugby title in a decade.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus stops short of blaming referee Andrea Piardi for Paris defeat
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus accepted responsibility for the 21-19 defeat to France in Paris, but much of his press conference was spent on the pressure a referee faces in front of a partisan home crowd. The Springboks dominated the scrum, and Erasmus conceded they may have asked too much of referee Andrea Piardi. He said the team had played themselves into a hole and the coaching staff must answer for it. He insisted he was not blaming Piardi. "I don't think there's much more to blame than ourselves," he said.
